claim: Monkey D. Luffy gained his rubber body by eating a Devil Fruit as a child.
explanation: Luffy accidentally ate the Gomu Gomu no Mi when he was young, which turned his body into rubber and cost him the ability to swim.

claim: Sanji was the first member to join Luffy's crew.
explanation: Roronoa Zoro was the first crewmate to join Luffy. Sanji joined later, after the Baratie events.

claim: Roronoa Zoro's ambition is to become the world's greatest swordsman.
explanation: Zoro's lifelong dream is to surpass every other swordsman, a goal tied to a promise he made as a child.

claim: Nami's dream is to find the legendary sea called the All Blue.
explanation: Finding the All Blue is Sanji's dream. Nami's dream is to draw a complete map of the world.

claim: Nami's dream is to draw a complete map of the entire world.
explanation: Nami serves as the Straw Hats' navigator and cartographer, and her stated ambition is to chart the whole world.

claim: Usopp's dream is to become a great doctor.
explanation: Usopp's dream is to become a brave warrior of the sea. Becoming a doctor is Chopper's dream.

claim: Usopp's father is Yasopp, a member of the Red-Haired Pirates.
explanation: Yasopp is the sniper of Shanks' crew and is Usopp's father.

claim: Sanji's dream is to find the All Blue, a sea where fish from all four seas gather.
explanation: Sanji, the Straw Hats' cook, wants to find the All Blue, a legendary sea said to hold fish from every ocean.

claim: Tony Tony Chopper was born a human and later became a reindeer after eating a Devil Fruit.
explanation: Chopper was born a reindeer. Eating the Hito Hito no Mi gave him human intelligence and the ability to take human-like forms.

claim: Franky is the shipwright who built the Thousand Sunny.
explanation: Franky joined as the Straw Hats' shipwright and built the Thousand Sunny using Adam Wood.

claim: Brook is a skeleton who returned to life after eating the Yomi Yomi no Mi.
explanation: The Yomi Yomi no Mi let Brook's soul return to his body after he died, and he was found as a living skeleton.

claim: Jinbe was the ninth member to join the Straw Hat Pirates.
explanation: Brook was the ninth member. Jinbe was the tenth. (Spoiler: Wano-era crew status.)

claim: Jinbe is a whale shark fish-man and a master of Fish-Man Karate.
explanation: Jinbe is a whale shark fish-man and Fish-Man Karate master who later became the Straw Hats' helmsman. (Spoiler: joins the crew.)

claim: Luffy's grandfather, Monkey D. Garp, is a notorious pirate.
explanation: Garp is a famous Marine Vice Admiral, known as the Hero of the Marines.

claim: Luffy's sworn brother Portgas D. Ace joined the Marines.
explanation: Ace became a pirate. He founded the Spade Pirates and later served as a division commander under Whitebeard.

claim: Nico Robin comes from Ohara, an island of scholars that the World Government destroyed.
explanation: Robin is a survivor of Ohara, whose archaeologists were targeted for researching the forbidden Void Century.

claim: Shanks gave the Gomu Gomu no Mi to Luffy as a gift.
explanation: Luffy ate the fruit without permission. It belonged to Shanks' crew, who had acquired it, and Shanks did not give it to him.

claim: Zoro made his promise to become the world's greatest swordsman with Kuina, a girl from his childhood dojo.
explanation: Zoro and Kuina were rivals who trained together at their dojo, and after Kuina's death Zoro carried their promise forward.

claim: Nami was forced to work as a cartographer for the Arlong Pirates.
explanation: Nami drew maps for Arlong's crew to try to buy back her home village.

claim: Kaya, whom the Straw Hats met in Syrup Village, gave them the Thousand Sunny.
explanation: Kaya gave them the Going Merry. The Thousand Sunny was built later by Franky.

claim: Nami's adoptive mother, Bellemere, was killed by Arlong.
explanation: Bellemere, a former Marine who raised Nami and Nojiko, was killed by Arlong, which shaped Nami's later life.

claim: Sanji's father, Vinsmoke Judge, is a Marine Admiral.
explanation: Judge is the head of the Vinsmoke family and leads the Germa Kingdom and Germa 66, not the Marines. (Spoiler: Whole Cake Island arc.)

claim: Sanji is the third son of Vinsmoke Judge and was born into the Germa Kingdom.
explanation: Sanji is Judge's third son, with Ichiji and Niji before him. (Spoiler: Whole Cake Island arc.)

claim: Usopp's mother, Banchina, died of an illness when he was a child.
explanation: Banchina died of illness while Usopp was still a young child, and the loss shaped his childhood.

claim: Chopper joined the Straw Hat Pirates during the Alabasta arc.
explanation: Chopper joined at the end of the Drum Island arc, before the Straw Hats reached Alabasta.

claim: Chopper was taken in by Dr. Hiluluk after being driven away by his herd.
explanation: Hiluluk took in Chopper and taught him medicine. Dr. Kureha trained him after Hiluluk died.

claim: Franky learned shipbuilding as a student of Tom, the master shipwright of Water 7.
explanation: Tom was a master shipwright, and Franky was one of his apprentices in Water 7.

claim: Franky was trained as a shipwright primarily by Iceburg.
explanation: Franky's mentor was Tom. Iceburg was a fellow apprentice of Tom's.

claim: Brook's former crew left the whale Laboon at Reverse Mountain, and Brook promised to return to him.
explanation: The Rumbar Pirates left Laboon at the Twin Cape and promised to come back. Brook is the last survivor of that crew.

claim: Jinbe officially became a Straw Hat before the two-year timeskip.
explanation: Jinbe is a late addition who joined well after the timeskip. (Spoiler: Wano-era events.)

claim: Luffy's father is the former Pirate King, Gol D. Roger.
explanation: Luffy's father is Monkey D. Dragon, the leader of the Revolutionary Army.

claim: Princess Vivi of Alabasta infiltrated Baroque Works under the alias Miss Wednesday.
explanation: Vivi infiltrated Baroque Works to learn its plans and protect her kingdom, using the alias Miss Wednesday.

claim: Red-Leg Zeff lost his leg in a duel with Dracule Mihawk.
explanation: Zeff lost his leg after he and the young Sanji were stranded on a rock, and he ate his own leg to survive while giving Sanji the remaining food.

claim: Before founding the Baratie, Zeff was a Marine known as Red-Leg.
explanation: Zeff was a pirate, not a Marine, before he became a restaurant owner.

claim: Nico Robin's mother, Olvia, was a Marine officer.
explanation: Olvia was an archaeologist from Ohara, not a Marine.

claim: Zoro's sword Wado Ichimonji was a gift from Dracule Mihawk.
explanation: Wado Ichimonji originally belonged to Kuina, Zoro's childhood rival, and Zoro came to use it as his own.

claim: In Baroque Works, Nico Robin used the alias Miss All Sunday.
explanation: Robin was the partner of Mr. 0 (Crocodile) in Baroque Works and went by Miss All Sunday.

claim: Zoro grew up in a dojo in Shimotsuki Village, located in the South Blue.
explanation: Zoro grew up in Shimotsuki Village, which is in the East Blue, not the South Blue.

claim: Franky's real name is Cutty Flam.
explanation: Cutty Flam is Franky's birth name. He later adopted the name Franky.

claim: Nico Robin received her first bounty when she was twenty years old.
explanation: Robin received her first bounty at the age of eight, which was 79,000,000 berries.

claim: Brook spent roughly fifty years drifting in the fog of the Florian Triangle before meeting the Straw Hats.
explanation: After his death, Brook's ship drifted for about fifty years in the fog before he met the Straw Hats at Thriller Bark.

claim: Sanji was born in the East Blue.
explanation: Sanji was born in the North Blue, where the Germa Kingdom is located. He later lived in the East Blue. (Spoiler: Whole Cake Island arc.)

claim: Jinbe was a member of the Sun Pirates, founded by the former slave Fisher Tiger.
explanation: Fisher Tiger was a former slave who freed other slaves and founded the Sun Pirates, which Jinbe joined. (Spoiler: Fish-Man Island arc.)

claim: Wapol, the former king of Drum Kingdom, was a Warlord of the Sea.
explanation: Wapol was only the king of Drum Kingdom and never held the Warlord title.

claim: Usopp's habit of telling lies began as a way to cheer up his sick mother.
explanation: As a child, Usopp made up tall tales to lift his ill mother's spirits, and the habit stuck.

claim: Monkey D. Garp turned down promotion to Admiral multiple times.
explanation: Garp refused promotion to Admiral and stayed at the rank of Vice Admiral.

claim: Yasopp is the first mate of the Red-Haired Pirates.
explanation: Benn Beckman is the first mate of the Red-Haired Pirates. Yasopp is the sniper.

claim: After the Enies Lobby arc, Luffy's bounty was raised to 500,000,000 berries.
explanation: After Enies Lobby, Luffy's bounty rose to 300,000,000 berries.

claim: Roronoa Zoro's bounty after the Wano Country arc is 1,111,000,000 berries.
explanation: Zoro's bounty rose to 1,111,000,000 berries after Wano. (Spoiler: Wano Country arc.)

claim: After the Wano Country arc, Sanji's bounty is higher than Zoro's.
explanation: Sanji's post-Wano bounty is 1,032,000,000 berries, which is lower than Zoro's 1,111,000,000. (Spoiler: Wano Country arc.)

claim: Sir Crocodile, a former Warlord of the Sea, ate the Suna Suna no Mi, which lets him turn into sand.
explanation: Crocodile's Suna Suna no Mi is a Logia-type Devil Fruit that gives him control over sand and the ability to dry things out.

claim: Marshall D. Teach, known as Blackbeard, has eaten two different Devil Fruits.
explanation: Teach ate the Yami Yami no Mi and later took the Gura Gura no Mi, an unprecedented feat. (Spoiler: Marineford arc.)

claim: Donquixote Doflamingo's Devil Fruit is the Mero Mero no Mi.
explanation: Doflamingo ate the Ito Ito no Mi, which lets him create and control strings. The Mero Mero no Mi belongs to Boa Hancock.

claim: Marine officer Smoker ate the Mera Mera no Mi.
explanation: Smoker ate the Moku Moku no Mi, which lets him turn into smoke. The Mera Mera no Mi is a fire-based fruit associated with Ace and later Sabo.

claim: Rob Lucci, a CP9 agent, has the Neko Neko no Mi, Model: Leopard.
explanation: Lucci's fruit is a Zoan-type Devil Fruit that lets him transform into a leopard and a hybrid form.

claim: Dracule Mihawk is a Marine Admiral.
explanation: Mihawk was a Warlord of the Sea, which was a position associated with the World Government but not a Marine rank. He is not an Admiral.

claim: Whitebeard's real name is Edward Newgate.
explanation: Edward Newgate, known as Whitebeard, led the Whitebeard Pirates and was once called the strongest man in the world.

claim: Buggy the Clown's Devil Fruit makes his body as hard as steel.
explanation: Buggy ate the Bara Bara no Mi, which lets him split his body into pieces and makes him immune to cutting attacks.

claim: Former Marine Admiral Aokiji (Kuzan) ate the Magu Magu no Mi.
explanation: Aokiji ate the Hie Hie no Mi, an ice-based Logia fruit. The Magu Magu no Mi belongs to Sakazuki (Akainu).

claim: Shanks, the leader of the Red-Haired Pirates, is one of the Four Emperors.
explanation: Shanks holds the title of Yonko, one of the most powerful pirates of the New World.

claim: The Cross Guild was founded by Crocodile, Dracule Mihawk and Donquixote Doflamingo.
explanation: The Cross Guild's key figures are Crocodile, Mihawk and Buggy, not Doflamingo. Doflamingo was imprisoned in Impel Down after Dressrosa. (Spoiler: post-Wano events.)

claim: Baroque Works agent Mr. 3, Galdino, has a Devil Fruit of the Logia type called the Doru Doru no Mi.
explanation: The Doru Doru no Mi is a Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that lets Galdino create and shape wax. It is not a Logia.

claim: Donquixote Doflamingo was born into the Celestial Dragons.
explanation: Doflamingo's family were Celestial Dragons living at Mary Geoise before his father renounced that status. (Spoiler: Dressrosa arc.)

claim: Donquixote Rosinante, also known as Corazon, was Doflamingo's older brother.
explanation: Rosinante was Doflamingo's younger brother. He later joined the Marines and infiltrated Doflamingo's crew. (Spoiler: Dressrosa arc.)

claim: While undercover in Water 7, CP9 agent Kalifa worked as a bartender.
explanation: Kalifa posed as the secretary of Iceburg, the mayor of Water 7 and head of Galley-La Company. Blueno was the agent who posed as a bartender.

claim: CP0 answers to the Marine Fleet Admiral.
explanation: CP0 is an intelligence agency under the World Government and serves the Five Elders directly. It is not part of the Marines' chain of command.

claim: Marshall D. Teach was a member of the Whitebeard Pirates before he betrayed the crew.
explanation: Teach served under Whitebeard for years before killing Thatch and leaving the crew. (Spoiler: Marineford backstory.)

claim: Blackbeard killed Thatch in order to steal the Gura Gura no Mi.
explanation: Teach killed Thatch to take the Yami Yami no Mi. He acquired the Gura Gura no Mi later, from Whitebeard's body. (Spoiler: Marineford arc.)

claim: Moby Dick is the name of Big Mom's flagship.
explanation: Moby Dick was the flagship of the Whitebeard Pirates, not Big Mom's ship.

claim: Shanks lost his right arm while saving Luffy from a Sea King.
explanation: Shanks lost his left arm saving young Luffy from a Sea King.

claim: In the Marine rank structure, Rear Admiral ranks above Vice Admiral.
explanation: Vice Admiral ranks above Rear Admiral. The ladder runs from Fleet Admiral and Admiral down through Vice Admiral and Rear Admiral.

claim: Sengoku held the position of Fleet Admiral before Sakazuki (Akainu).
explanation: Sengoku was Fleet Admiral during the Marineford war, and Sakazuki took the position afterward. (Spoiler: post-Marineford events.)

claim: Aokiji (Kuzan) became Fleet Admiral after the Marineford war.
explanation: Sakazuki (Akainu) became Fleet Admiral. Kuzan left the Marines after losing the position to him. (Spoiler: post-Marineford events.)

claim: The Seven Warlords of the Sea system was abolished after the Dressrosa arc.
explanation: The World Government abolished the Warlord system in the aftermath of the Dressrosa events. (Spoiler: Dressrosa and Reverie aftermath.)

claim: Bartholomew Kuma, a former Warlord, was once a member of the Revolutionary Army.
explanation: Kuma had served in the Revolutionary Army before becoming a Warlord. (Spoiler: later Sabaody and Egghead-era lore.)

claim: Gecko Moria's Kage Kage no Mi allows him to steal souls.
explanation: The Kage Kage no Mi lets Moria steal people's shadows, not souls. Stolen shadows are placed into corpses to create zombies.

claim: Sabo serves as the Revolutionary Army's Chief of Staff.
explanation: Sabo holds the position of Chief of Staff in the Revolutionary Army under Monkey D. Dragon. (Spoiler: Dressrosa arc and later.)

claim: Eustass Kid's Devil Fruit is the Jiki Jiki no Mi, which gives him magnetic powers.
explanation: Kid ate the Jiki Jiki no Mi, a Paramecia-type fruit that lets him control magnetism.

claim: Trafalgar Law's Devil Fruit is the Ope Ope no Mi.
explanation: Law ate the Ope Ope no Mi, which lets him create a spherical Room and manipulate everything within it.

claim: Scratchmen Apoo is the captain of the Hawk Pirates.
explanation: Apoo is the captain of the On Air Pirates, one of the Worst Generation crews.

claim: Charlotte Katakuri ate the Mochi Mochi no Mi.
explanation: Katakuri's Mochi Mochi no Mi is a special Paramecia fruit that lets him create and control mochi. (Spoiler: Whole Cake Island arc.)

claim: Big Mom's Devil Fruit is the Gura Gura no Mi.
explanation: Charlotte Linlin ate the Soru Soru no Mi, which lets her manipulate souls. The Gura Gura no Mi was Whitebeard's.

claim: Kaido ate the Uo Uo no Mi, Model: Seiryu.
explanation: Kaido's fruit is a mythical Zoan that lets him transform into an Azure Dragon. (Spoiler: Wano Country arc.)

claim: Blackbeard was already a Yonko at the time of the Marineford war.
explanation: Teach rose to the rank of Yonko after Marineford, once he had taken the Gura Gura no Mi and built his crew's power. (Spoiler: post-Marineford events.)

claim: Mary Geoise, home of the Celestial Dragons, sits on top of the Red Line.
explanation: Mary Geoise is the capital of the World Government and stands on the Red Line, the continent that encircles the world.

claim: During the Impel Down arc, the Chief Warden of Impel Down was Magellan.
explanation: Magellan served as Impel Down's warden, with Hannyabal as his deputy, during the Impel Down events. (Spoiler: Impel Down arc.)

claim: Doflamingo's father, Donquixote Homing, gave up his status as a Celestial Dragon.
explanation: Homing renounced his status and took his family to live among commoners, which led to years of hardship for them. (Spoiler: Dressrosa arc.)

claim: CP9 agent Kaku has the Ushi Ushi no Mi, Model: Giraffe.
explanation: Kaku's Zoan fruit lets him turn into a giraffe, and he used it alongside his Rokushiki techniques.

claim: Spandam was the director of CP0 during the Enies Lobby arc.
explanation: Spandam was the chief of CP9 during the Enies Lobby arc, not of CP0.

claim: Vergo, an officer in Doflamingo's organization, was secretly a Marine.
explanation: Vergo was a Marine Vice Admiral working undercover in Doflamingo's group. (Spoiler: Punk Hazard and Dressrosa arcs.)

claim: Enel's Devil Fruit is the Goro Goro no Mi, a Logia fruit that gives him lightning powers.
explanation: Enel, the self-proclaimed god of Skypiea, ate the Goro Goro no Mi and can turn into and control lightning.

claim: Crocodile's Baroque Works plan was aimed at acquiring the ancient weapon Poseidon.
explanation: Crocodile sought the ancient weapon Pluton, which he believed was hidden in Alabasta. Poseidon is a different ancient weapon.

claim: Baroque Works' Mr. 1, Daz Bones, ate the Supa Supa no Mi, which makes his body into blades.
explanation: Daz Bones' Supa Supa no Mi is a Paramecia fruit that lets him turn any part of his body into steel blades.

claim: Admiral Fujitora is the Fleet Admiral of the Marines.
explanation: Fujitora (Issho) holds the rank of Admiral, one of the Marines' top three field commanders. The Fleet Admiral is Sakazuki (Akainu). (Spoiler: Dressrosa-era and later.)

claim: Donquixote Rosinante ate the Nagi Nagi no Mi, which let him create a field of silence.
explanation: Rosinante's Nagi Nagi no Mi allowed him to make a soundproof area around himself. (Spoiler: Dressrosa arc backstory.)

claim: Shanks was once a member of the Rocks Pirates.
explanation: Shanks served as a boy on the Roger Pirates, not the Rocks Pirates.

claim: Admiral Ryokugyu (Aramaki) has the Mori Mori no Mi, a Logia fruit tied to plants and forests.
explanation: Ryokugyu's Mori Mori no Mi lets him create and control plants and forests. (Spoiler: post-timeskip Marines.)

claim: Dracule Mihawk served as a Marine before becoming a Warlord.
explanation: Mihawk was not a Marine. He was a lone swordsman who was named a Warlord.

claim: Charlotte Linlin and Kaido were both members of the Rocks Pirates in their youth.
explanation: The Rocks Pirates, led by Rocks D. Xebec, included young Linlin and Kaido, along with Edward Newgate. (Spoiler: Rocks Pirates backstory.)

claim: Boa Hancock became a Warlord of the Sea only after the Marineford war.
explanation: Hancock was already a Warlord when Luffy reached Amazon Lily, before Marineford. (Spoiler: Amazon Lily and Marineford arcs.)

claim: Luffy's Gomu Gomu no Mi turns his body into rubber, which makes him resistant to electricity.
explanation: The Gomu Gomu no Mi is a Paramecia fruit. Rubber insulates against electrical attacks, though it does not protect him from everything.

claim: A Devil Fruit user can swim normally as long as they stay in shallow water.
explanation: Devil Fruit users lose the ability to swim in any sea water, and the depth does not matter. Fresh-water baths and shallow puddles are also dangerous in some cases.

claim: The sword Wado Ichimonji originally belonged to Kuina, Zoro's childhood rival, before he carried it.
explanation: After Kuina's death, her sword passed to Zoro, who promised to become the world's greatest swordsman. Wado Ichimonji is one of his three swords.

claim: The Thousand Sunny was the Straw Hat Pirates' first ship.
explanation: The Going Merry was their first ship, given by Kaya. The Thousand Sunny was built later by Franky after the Water 7 and Enies Lobby events.

claim: The Going Merry was a gift to the Straw Hats from Kaya, a wealthy girl from Syrup Village.
explanation: Kaya gave the caravel to Luffy and his crew after the Black Cat Pirates incident. Usopp then joined as a crew member.

claim: Seastone neutralizes the powers of a Devil Fruit user who touches it.
explanation: Seastone (Kairoseki) emits the same energy as the sea, so contact removes a Devil Fruit user's abilities and strength while touching it.

claim: Tony Tony Chopper's Hito Hito no Mi is a Logia-type Devil Fruit.
explanation: It is a Zoan fruit that gives Chopper human traits and forms. Logia fruits instead let the user turn into a natural element.

claim: Portgas D. Ace's Mera Mera no Mi is a Logia-type Devil Fruit that creates and becomes fire.
explanation: The Mera Mera no Mi lets its user turn into and control fire. It is a Logia fruit.

claim: Only Devil Fruit users are able to learn Haki.
explanation: Haki is an ability that anyone can develop, including people with no Devil Fruit. Characters such as Zoro and Sanji use Haki without eating a Devil Fruit.

claim: Franky built the Thousand Sunny using wood from Adam Wood, the Treasure Tree Adam.
explanation: Adam Wood is from the Treasure Tree Adam, a legendary tree known for its durability. Franky used it to build the Straw Hats' second ship.

claim: Observation Haki allows a user to sense the presence and emotions of others, and can even help anticipate attacks.
explanation: Observation Haki (Kenbunshoku) lets the user sense presences and feelings, even without seeing them. Advanced users can glimpse a short moment ahead.

claim: Armament Haki can only be used for attacking and cannot be used for defense.
explanation: Armament Haki (Busoshoku) creates an invisible armor that is used for both offense and defense. It can also strengthen weapons.

claim: Conqueror's Haki is a rare ability that only a small number of people possess.
explanation: Only one in many millions is said to be born with it. It can knock out opponents with weaker wills.

claim: Zoan Devil Fruits only allow users to turn into mammals.
explanation: Zoan fruits include animal forms beyond mammals, as well as mythical creatures. Birds such as Marco's phoenix are shown in canon.

claim: Logia users can usually turn their bodies intangible, but attacks infused with Armament Haki can still hit them.
explanation: Logia users pass most normal attacks through their elemental bodies. Haki attacks and Seastone are established ways to bypass this.

claim: Crocodile's Suna Suna no Mi is a Zoan-type Devil Fruit.
explanation: The Suna Suna no Mi is a Logia fruit that turns the user into sand and lets him control it.

claim: Trafalgar Law's Ope Ope no Mi is a Paramecia fruit that lets him create a spherical area called a Room.
explanation: Inside the Room, Law can manipulate objects and people. The size of the Room is limited by his stamina.

claim: The Yomi Yomi no Mi allows Brook to come back to life an unlimited number of times.
explanation: The fruit gave Brook a single resurrection after death. It does not make him able to revive repeatedly.

claim: Blackbeard's Yami Yami no Mi can nullify the powers of other Devil Fruit users on contact.
explanation: The Yami Yami no Mi is a Logia that cancels Devil Fruit abilities it touches. The user also takes damage that Logia users normally avoid, since he cannot avoid hits.

claim: Whitebeard's Gura Gura no Mi is a Logia-type Devil Fruit.
explanation: It is a Paramecia fruit that gives the user the power to create earthquakes. It does not turn the body into an element.

claim: The Thousand Sunny's Coup de Burst launches the ship by releasing compressed air.
explanation: Franky's Coup de Burst expels a blast of compressed air to send the ship flying. It was built into the Sunny and is not a Devil Fruit power.

claim: Franky's use of cola as fuel is a Devil Fruit ability.
explanation: Franky is a cyborg who built his own body. He is not a Devil Fruit user, and cola is the energy source for his technology.

claim: Poneglyphs are extremely durable stones written in an ancient script that Nico Robin can read.
explanation: They record hidden history and are almost impossible to destroy. Robin learned to read the script in Ohara.

claim: Poneglyphs are written in the common script of the world and can be read by any literate person.
explanation: Poneglyphs use an ancient script that very few people can read. The World Government banned research into them.

claim: A Vivre Card is made from a piece of its owner and moves toward that person.
explanation: Vivre Cards are made from a clipping of the owner's nail. They shift toward the owner and shrink or burn as the owner's life dwindles.

claim: A standard Log Pose points directly to Laugh Tale from the start of the Grand Line.
explanation: A Log Pose locks onto the next island's magnetic field in the chain. Reaching Laugh Tale requires more than a Log Pose.

claim: Dials are shells from Skypiea that can store and release energy such as wind or impact.
explanation: Dials absorb and store different forms of energy. Franky and others have built tools using them.

claim: Seastone only affects Logia users and has no effect on Paramecia or Zoan users.
explanation: Seastone affects every Devil Fruit user, regardless of fruit type. Contact removes powers and weakens the body.

claim: The Pacifista are cyborgs modeled after Bartholomew Kuma.
explanation: The World Government's Pacifista were built using Kuma's design. They are not Devil Fruit users, although some can fire laser beams.

claim: Sabo ate Ace's Mera Mera no Mi after Ace's death.
explanation: SPOILER (Dressrosa): after a Devil Fruit user dies, the fruit reappears elsewhere. Sabo won the Mera Mera no Mi in the Corrida Colosseum tournament.

claim: Bartholomew Kuma's Nikyu Nikyu no Mi is a Zoan-type Devil Fruit.
explanation: The Nikyu Nikyu no Mi is a Paramecia fruit. It lets the user repel nearly anything they touch.

claim: Kizaru's Pika Pika no Mi is a Logia that turns his body into light.
explanation: The Pika Pika no Mi lets the user create, control, and become light. It is categorized as a Logia fruit.

claim: Zoro's sword Shusui originally belonged to Kozuki Oden.
explanation: Shusui was originally the sword of the samurai Ryuma. Zoro obtained it later.

claim: Sandai Kitetsu is said to be a cursed sword.
explanation: Legend holds that it brings misfortune to its owner. Zoro carries it among his swords.

claim: The Going Merry was sunk by the Marines during the war at Marineford.
explanation: The Going Merry was retired and given a farewell after the Straw Hats' Water 7 events. It was not present at Marineford.

claim: Ryuo is an advanced application of Armament Haki.
explanation: SPOILER (Wano): Ryuo is a refined technique built on Armament Haki. It is not the same as Conqueror's Haki.

claim: Seeing a moment of the future with Observation Haki is only possible for Devil Fruit users.
explanation: Advanced Observation Haki is a trained ability and does not depend on a Devil Fruit. Users such as Katakuri show it without any fruit tied to the power.

claim: Doflamingo's awakened Ito Ito no Mi allowed him to turn parts of his surroundings into strings.
explanation: SPOILER (Dressrosa): awakening lets a user affect the environment, not just their own body. The Ito Ito no Mi is a Paramecia fruit.

claim: Katakuri's Mochi Mochi no Mi is classified as a Logia fruit.
explanation: The Mochi Mochi no Mi is a special Paramecia fruit. Katakuri can create and control mochi, but it is not a Logia.

claim: Luffy's true Devil Fruit is the Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Nika, a Mythical Zoan.
explanation: SPOILER (Wano): the World Government hid the fruit's true identity. It is not a Paramecia, despite its appearance as a rubber fruit.

claim: Marco's Tori Tori no Mi, Model: Phoenix is an Ancient Zoan.
explanation: It is a Mythical Zoan fruit, not an Ancient Zoan. It gives Marco phoenix forms and regenerative flames.

claim: Kaido's Uo Uo no Mi, Model: Seiryu is a Mythical Zoan that turns him into an azure dragon.
explanation: SPOILER (Wano): Kaido's fruit gave him a dragon form. It is a Mythical Zoan, not a regular fish-based fruit.

claim: When a Devil Fruit user dies, the fruit reappears as a new fruit somewhere in the world.
explanation: This is an established rule of Devil Fruits. The new fruit can be found and eaten by someone else.

claim: Mihawk's black blade Yoru is classified as a Great Grade sword.
explanation: Yoru is one of the twelve Supreme Grade swords. Supreme Grade is the highest tier of the Meito ranking.

claim: Devil Fruit awakening is exclusive to Logia-type fruits.
explanation: Awakenings have been shown for Paramecia and Zoan users as well. Doflamingo's Ito Ito no Mi is a Paramecia example.

claim: Wado Ichimonji is classified as a Supreme Grade sword in the Meito ranking.
explanation: SPOILER (Wano): Wado Ichimonji is a Great Grade sword, the second-highest tier. The Supreme Grade is the top tier and has only twelve swords.

claim: Conqueror's Haki can never be combined with Armament Haki in the same attack.
explanation: SPOILER (Wano): Luffy and Kaido showed attacks that combine the two. This is an advanced application of Armament Haki infused with Conqueror's Haki.

claim: SMILE fruits were created by Vegapunk.
explanation: SMILE fruits were created by Caesar Clown, not by Vegapunk. They give Zoan-like powers but produce a laughing side effect.

claim: Chopper's Rumble Ball has a permanent effect once eaten.
explanation: The Rumble Ball only lasts for a limited time, after which Chopper reverts to normal. It lets him access extra forms in that time.

claim: Enma drains Armament Haki from its wielder when used.
explanation: SPOILER (Wano): Enma draws on Armament Haki, and Zoro nearly exhausts his Haki using it. It originally belonged to Kozuki Oden.

claim: Shanks gave Monkey D. Luffy his straw hat before leaving East Blue.
explanation: Shanks entrusted the hat to young Luffy and told him to return it once he became a great pirate. It became Luffy's signature item.

claim: Nami grew up in Syrup Village.
explanation: Nami grew up in Cocoyasi Village on the Conomi Islands. Syrup Village is where Usopp and Kaya lived.

claim: Crocodile, a Warlord of the Sea, secretly led Baroque Works and plotted to take over Alabasta.
explanation: Crocodile planned to seize the kingdom for its hidden Ancient Weapon. The Straw Hats stopped his coup.

claim: Skypiea is a sky island located in the East Blue.
explanation: Skypiea is in the sky above the Grand Line, reached by the Knock Up Stream near Jaya. It is not in East Blue.

claim: CP9 took Nico Robin to Enies Lobby, and the Straw Hats followed to rescue her.
explanation: SPOILER (Water 7/Enies Lobby): the crew attacked the World Government's judicial island to save Robin from CP9.

claim: Gecko Moria, the master of Thriller Bark, was one of the Four Emperors.
explanation: Moria was a Warlord of the Sea, not one of the Four Emperors.

claim: Fish-Man Island is located about 10,000 meters below sea level, near the Red Line.
explanation: Ships need coating and a special route to reach it. It lies at the bottom of the Grand Line's sea, under the Red Line.

claim: The Sabaody Archipelago is located in the New World.
explanation: Sabaody is in the first half of the Grand Line, at the foot of the Red Line. The New World lies beyond Fish-Man Island.

claim: Edward Newgate, known as Whitebeard, died during the Battle of Marineford.
explanation: SPOILER (Marineford): Whitebeard died standing in the battle after protecting his crew. His death changed the balance of power in the New World.

claim: Monkey D. Dragon, the Revolutionary Army leader, is Luffy's uncle.
explanation: Dragon is Luffy's father. Garp is Luffy's grandfather.

claim: The island of Ohara was destroyed by a Buster Call because its scholars researched the Void Century.
explanation: The World Government ordered the Buster Call after discovering Ohara's research into the forbidden history.

claim: Nico Robin was already an adult when Ohara was destroyed.
explanation: Robin was a child of about eight years old at the time. She was the only scholar to escape the Buster Call.

claim: Level 6 of Impel Down is called Eternal Hell.
explanation: Level 6 holds the most dangerous prisoners and is the lowest standard floor of the prison.

claim: Whitebeard went to war with the Marines at Marineford to rescue Luffy.
explanation: SPOILER (Marineford): Whitebeard went to rescue Portgas D. Ace, who was to be executed. Luffy joined separately to save his brother.

claim: After the Straw Hats were scattered at Sabaody, they reunited two years later at the same archipelago.
explanation: Kuma sent each crew member to different locations, and they trained during the time skip. They returned to Sabaody before heading to Fish-Man Island.

claim: Kuma sent Zoro to Amazon Lily after the Sabaody scattering.
explanation: Luffy was sent to Amazon Lily. Zoro landed on Kuraigana Island, where Mihawk lived.

claim: Hody Jones led the New Fish-Man Pirates against Fish-Man Island.
explanation: SPOILER (Fish-Man Island): Hody sought revenge against humans and attempted a coup.

claim: Fujitora served as the Fleet Admiral during the Dressrosa arc.
explanation: Fujitora (Issho) was an Admiral. Sakazuki (Akainu) was the Fleet Admiral.

claim: Sanji's arranged engagement to Charlotte Pudding was meant to seal an alliance between Big Mom and the Vinsmoke family.
explanation: SPOILER (Whole Cake Island): the marriage was political, and the Straw Hats rescued Sanji from it.

claim: Sanji is the son of Big Mom.
explanation: SPOILER (Whole Cake Island): Sanji is the son of Vinsmoke Judge of the Germa Kingdom.

claim: Donquixote Doflamingo ruled Dressrosa as king while also being a Warlord of the Sea.
explanation: SPOILER (Dressrosa): Doflamingo secretly controlled the kingdom and hid his control behind a false history.

claim: The Beasts Pirates are the crew of Charlotte Linlin, known as Big Mom.
explanation: Big Mom leads the Big Mom Pirates. The Beasts Pirates are led by Kaido.

claim: The island of Zou is located on the back of a giant elephant named Zunesha.
explanation: Zunesha walks the sea and carries the Mink Tribe's home on its back.

claim: Kozuki Oden was the shogun of Wano Country.
explanation: SPOILER (Wano): Oden was the daimyo of Kuri. Kurozumi Orochi held the shogun position.

claim: Spandam gave the order for the Buster Call on Enies Lobby.
explanation: SPOILER (Enies Lobby): the CP9 leader ordered it after the Straw Hats attacked. The Marines' ships then fired on the island.

claim: Nico Robin joined the Straw Hats during the Enies Lobby arc.
explanation: Robin joined the crew after Alabasta. Enies Lobby was the arc where she was taken from them and rescued.

claim: Iceburg was mayor of Water 7 and president of the Galley-La Company.
explanation: He was also the apprentice of Tom, the shipwright who built Gold Roger's ship.

claim: Eneru, the self-proclaimed god of Skypiea, was defeated by Zoro.
explanation: Luffy defeated Eneru. His rubber body let him fight a lightning user.

claim: Wano Country had been isolated from the outside world for centuries.
explanation: Wano is closed off by its location and its laws. It was opened up after the events of the Wano arc.

claim: Brook joined the Straw Hats before the Enies Lobby arc.
explanation: Brook joined at Thriller Bark, which comes after Enies Lobby in the story.

claim: The Void Century is a 100-year gap in recorded history, and the World Government forbids researching it.
explanation: What happened during it is only partly revealed. The ban on research was the reason for the Ohara incident.

claim: The three Ancient Weapons are Pluton, Poseidon, and Mars.
explanation: The third weapon is Uranus, not Mars. Pluton is a warship, and Poseidon is linked to a mermaid princess.

claim: The Road Poneglyphs, when combined, reveal the location of Laugh Tale.
explanation: There are four Road Poneglyphs. Collecting them leads to the final island, Laugh Tale.

claim: The meaning of the D. in the Will of D. has been fully explained in the manga.
explanation: The full meaning is still unresolved. Canon has only hinted at its importance, so any complete explanation is theory.

claim: The Ancient Weapon Poseidon is connected to Princess Shirahoshi.
explanation: SPOILER (Fish-Man Island): Poseidon is tied to the mermaid princess, who is able to command Sea Kings.

claim: Mary Geoise is located at the bottom of the sea, near Fish-Man Island.
explanation: Mary Geoise sits atop the Red Line, at the top of the world. It is home to the World Government's Celestial Dragons.

claim: Sabo is the Chief of Staff of the Revolutionary Army.
explanation: SPOILER (Dressrosa and later): Sabo is Dragon's second-in-command in the organization.

claim: The Reverie at Mary Geoise is held every year.
explanation: It is held once every four years. Leaders of the world's member kingdoms gather for it.

claim: Gol D. Roger was executed in Loguetown.
explanation: His execution began the Great Pirate Era. Loguetown is known as the town of beginning and end.

claim: Gol D. Roger was captured by the Marines at Marineford before his execution.
explanation: Roger turned himself in to the Marines. His execution was held in Loguetown, not at Marineford.

claim: Marshall D. Teach killed Thatch and took the Yami Yami no Mi.
explanation: SPOILER (Marineford): Teach was a Whitebeard Pirate who betrayed the crew to take the fruit. This led to Ace chasing him.

claim: Impel Down is located directly beneath Marineford.
explanation: Impel Down is a prison in the Calm Belt, separate from Marineford. Prisoners are sent there by Marine ships.

claim: The World Government has recognized Buggy as one of the Four Emperors.
explanation: SPOILER (post-Wano): Buggy was named a Yonko after the Wano events. Many fans see this as an unusual outcome.

claim: Silvers Rayleigh is a member of the Revolutionary Army.
explanation: Rayleigh was Roger's first mate and later lived in Sabaody. He trained Luffy but did not join the Revolutionary Army.

claim: Fisher Tiger freed slaves from Mary Geoise before founding the Sun Pirates.
explanation: SPOILER (Fish-Man Island): he was a former slave who freed others and later led the Sun Pirates.

claim: Monkey D. Luffy is confirmed to be a descendant of Gol D. Roger.
explanation: Canon identifies Luffy's father as Dragon and does not confirm a descent from Roger. Ace is Roger's son.

claim: Nico Olvia, an Ohara scholar, was Nico Robin's mother.
explanation: SPOILER (Ohara): Olvia was a scholar who stayed behind to protect the knowledge of the island and helped Robin escape.

claim: Princess Shirahoshi of Fish-Man Island is a human.
explanation: Shirahoshi is a mermaid. She is the daughter of King Neptune and Queen Otohime.

claim: Silvers Rayleigh served as the first mate of the Roger Pirates.
explanation: He was nicknamed the Dark King and was Roger's closest right-hand man.

claim: The Red Line is located in the Calm Belt.
explanation: The Red Line is a continent that runs around the world. The Calm Belts are separate sea regions on either side of the Grand Line.
